newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Fujimori cancels Bolivia trip - palace.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Fujimori cancels Bolivia trip - palace.

text.p: Peru's President Alberto Fujimori on Saturday cancelled a scheduled three-day trip to Bolivia, whose ambassador to Lima -- one of 72 hostages held by Marxist rebels -- is reportedly showing signs of emotional breakdown.
A government spokeswoman told Reuters that Fujimori called off the trip to meet Bolivian President Gonzalo Sanchez de Lozada until further notice but did not give a reason.
Instead, the president travelled on Saturday morning to southern Peru to inspect public works near the town of Marcona, 220 miles (350 kms) south of the capital, she said.
The spokeswoman said Fujimori, who had been slated to travel to La Paz in the afternoon, now plans to visit Bolivia next week but no date has been set.

French President Jacques Chirac, on a tour of the four member nations of the Mercosur customs union, was due to fly to La Paz on Saturday but it was not known if Fujimori cancelled his visit to avoid a possible conflict of schedules.
Fujimori's trip to Bolivia would have been his second to the neighbouring Andean country since the start of the 88-day hostage siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
Earlier this week, La Paz's envoy to Lima, Jorge Gumucio, quarreled with a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebel inside the besieged diplomatic compound, a police source said.
In the most serious episode of its kind known to have happened during the siege, the MRTA rebel threatened Gumucio with a gun before other hostages intervened to calm the ambassador, the source said.
Peruvian media said Gumucio suffered an attack of hysteria but La Paz officials said the ambassador reacted calmly when provoked by the rebel's "offensive" statements about Bolivia.

There have been frequent appeals on health grounds for the release of Gumucio, who is diabetic and has a history of heart and blood pressure problems. But the rebels have held on to the only hostage from a country other than Peru and Japan in the hope of exchanging him for MRTA members jailed in Bolivia.
